review: 1:3–1:4 בִּרְצוֹן לֵב … כּוֹס מָוֶת וָחֵמָה — the Arabic بِالرِّضَى عَنَّا شَرِبْتَ is 'You drank willingly for us'; Hebrew fronts the willing heart and leaves the cup on the cadence, as in hymn 43.
2:4 לְךָ נָשִׁיא — 'to You we bring'; the verb is the hiph'il of נשׂא used for offering (Ps 96:8, שְׂאוּ מִנְחָה), and it fills four syllables without the awkward נָשִׁים ('women').
3:2 שְׁלֵמָה לְעוֹלָמִים — 'complete forever'; the Arabic لِلتَّمَامِ أَبَدِيًّا is 'unto full completion eternally', and the two words carry both ideas.

4:2 תִּשָּׂא מֵעֵבֶר שֵׂכֶל — 'soars beyond understanding'; the Arabic يَسْمُو فَوْقَ إِدْرَاكِ الْأَنَام is a comparison, and Hebrew keeps the verb of rising with the abstract 'understanding' (Eph 3:19, מֵעַל לְדַעַת).
4:4 הַמֵּתִים בַּפְּשָׁעִים — Ephesians 2:1 (מֵתִים בְּפִשְׁעֵיכֶם); the Arabic مَيْتًا بِالْآثَام is that verse, pluralised to match 'those'.
